name: Squaremouth
description: America's largest travel insurance comparison marketplace, letting travellers quote and buy 100+ policies from 20 top insurers in one place. Its own affiliate program is open to anyone with no minimum commitment, pays commission on every referred policy sale through a 60-day cookie, and states explicitly that it does not cap earnings (non-licensed referrers earn up to $50 per sale).

evidence.summary: Official affiliate page FAQ, 'Is There A Limit To How Much I Can Make?': 'Squaremouth does not set a cap on your potential earnings. The more you refer, the more you can make. Non-licensed referrers can make up to $50 per sale. Licensed referrers may qualify for a volume-based commission structure.' The page also lists 'No minimum commitments and no cap on earning potential' as a program benefit.

Program mechanics from the official page: free to join, anyone eligible with no minimum commitments or qualifications, sign-up in minutes with same-day earning, 60-day cookie lifetime, real-time reporting dashboard, payment by ACH direct deposit once accrued credits exceed $50, paid within 45 days after month-end. The page names small social media influencers, bloggers and independent creators with a travel audience as partners. No percentage commission rate is published on the page, so commission_rate is null.
The official page gives the affiliate team email affiliates@squaremouth.com for account structuring questions, and shows the company address in Summit, NJ.

reasons.compensation: Explicit no-cap statement on the brand's own page ('does not set a cap on your potential earnings'); held below maximum because no percentage rate is published and non-licensed referrers are limited to $50 per individual sale.
reasons.contact_access: A named affiliate-team email (affiliates@squaremouth.com) is published on the official program page.
reasons.credibility: 20+ years in business, describes itself as America's largest travel insurance marketplace, 4.9/5 from 55,204 ratings shown on the page.
reasons.niche_fit: Travel insurance is a natural add-on for travel creators selling trips, itineraries and travel-safety content.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Anyone can join with no minimum commitments or qualifications, sign-up in minutes and same-day earning.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The official page explicitly names small social media influencers, bloggers and independent creators as partners, though the product is a quote widget/link rather than physical-product UGC.

name: Suunto
description: Finnish sports-watch and dive-computer brand for runners, triathletes and outdoor athletes, with average order values above $300. Its affiliate program pays a 10% base commission (top performers up to 15% with brand approval) on confirmed sales, with a 30-day cookie and monthly payouts, and explicitly welcomes creators, bloggers and social media partners.

evidence.summary: Official US program page FAQ, 'How much can I earn?': 'Base commission starts at 10%. Top-performing affiliates earn up to 15% with brand approval.' The 15% is a rate ceiling for approved top performers, not the base rate; the page also states average order value above $300, a 30-day cookie window, monthly payouts and free joining. No earnings-cap statement appears anywhere on the page, so commission_cap is unknown.

The page says 'Anyone. We welcome creators, publishers, bloggers, and social media partners' (all applications reviewed), sign-up is via 'one of our affiliate platforms' (the platforms are not named on the page), and support is via affiliate@suunto.com.

affiliate.network: Brand direct (via affiliate platforms, unnamed on page)

reasons.compensation: 10% base commission on an average order value above $300 is strong per-sale pay; the up-to-15% figure is a ceiling for approved top performers and no cap statement is published.
reasons.contact_access: A dedicated affiliate support email (affiliate@suunto.com) is published on the official page.
reasons.credibility: Long-established premium sports-watch brand with a global retail presence.
reasons.niche_fit: GPS watches are core gear for running, triathlon and outdoor fitness creators.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open to anyone with applications reviewed for alignment; free to join.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Creators, bloggers and social media partners are explicitly welcomed, though the program is link/code based rather than a structured UGC campaign program.

description: Social-media-first luxe activewear and swim brand whose styles have been worn by major Instagram celebrities and whose content is mostly user-generated. Its Awin affiliate program pays 10% commission on net sales with a 30-day cookie, monthly payments and real-time reporting; applications are reviewed and coupon/deal sites are not allowed.

evidence.summary: Official Awin merchant profile for 437 (US): 'We offer a 10% commission on net sales, excluding shipping, taxes and returns', 30-day cookie/conversion window, payments every 30 days, real-time reporting; blogs/sites/publications are reviewed for approval and coupons, discounts, deals and cashback sites are not allowed. No earnings-cap statement is published, so commission_cap is unknown.

The Awin profile describes 437 as 'a social media-first brand' and states 'Most of our content is user-generated as we believe they are the most powerful marketers', inviting publishers to 'put in a good word for us on your platform and earn money while you're at it'. Affiliate management contact given as careers@shop437.com.

reasons.compensation: Flat 10% on net sales via Awin is a solid, clearly published rate; no cap statement is published.
reasons.contact_access: An affiliate management email (careers@shop437.com) is published on the Awin profile, though it is a general careers address rather than a dedicated partnerships inbox.
reasons.credibility: Well-known social-first activewear label worn by major celebrities, but a smaller company than the global sportswear majors.
reasons.niche_fit: Activewear and swim are core fitness/fashion creator categories and the brand is built around social content.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Applications are reviewed for approval and coupon/deal/cashback publishers are excluded, which narrows who can join.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The brand states most of its content is user-generated and explicitly frames creators as its marketers — strong UGC evidence.

name: Glamourange
description: Luxury-fashion retailer focused on sunglasses, eyewear and tailored apparel, running a global influencer/ambassador affiliate program. Commission is tiered by audience size — 10% for nano creators (400–10K followers) up to 25% for mega influencers, 30% for existing customers and 35% for brand ambassadors — paid via PayPal. Its 'no maximum' wording covers the number of referrals, not an earnings cap, so the cap is honestly unknown.

evidence.summary: Official affiliate FAQ commission table: Tier 1 Nano influencers/inspirers (400–10K followers) 10%, Tier 2 Micro (10K–100K) 15%, Tier 3 Macro (100K–1M) 20%, Tier 4 Mega (1M+) 25%, Tier 5 existing customers 30%, Tier 6 brand ambassadors 35%, Tier 7 blogs/YouTube/websites/podcasts/print 15%. The recorded 10% is the starting social-creator tier.

The FAQ says 'No maximum number of referrals you can refer. We want you to earn more money' — a statement about referral COUNT, not an earnings cap, so per the directory standard commission_cap stays unknown. Program is free and global, applications reviewed in 1–5 business days on follower and engagement metrics, commissions paid by direct deposit to PayPal.

reasons.compensation: 10% starting rate for nano creators rising to 35% for ambassadors is generous on paper; no earnings-cap statement is published (only a no-maximum-referrals statement).
reasons.contact_access: No partnerships email is published on the FAQ page — contact is via a website form only.
reasons.credibility: Small, little-known luxury retailer; the fetched FAQ is served from the brand's Ghana locale and independent track record is thin.
reasons.niche_fit: Sunglasses and fashion outfits are natural fashion-creator content, though the catalogue is narrower than full-range fashion brands.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Free and global with a low 400-follower entry tier, but applications are reviewed on follower and engagement metrics.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The program is explicitly built for influencers, inspirers and ambassadors promoting on social media, blogs and YouTube.

name: Stasher
description: The world's largest luggage-storage platform, with 10,200+ vetted Stashpoints in hotels and shops across 1,200+ cities, letting travellers store bags for half the price of station lockers. Its affiliate program (run on Tapfiliate) pays 10% recurring commission on bookings with a 30-day cookie, monthly payouts from a £50 threshold, and explicitly lists social media creators among its channels.

evidence.summary: Stasher's official program listing on its Tapfiliate portal: 'Commission, 10% Recurring', cookie duration 30 days, payment monthly via PayPal and bank transfer with a £50 payout threshold, worldwide geography, channels include travel blogs, city guides and 'Social Media Creators'. Join portal is stasher.tapfiliate.com. No earnings-cap statement is published, so commission_cap is unknown.
The brand's homepage states 4.94 from 1.5M+ worldwide ratings, 10,200+ Stashpoints, millions of bags stored, and every booking includes insurance cover up to $1,000 per bag (per the program listing).

reasons.compensation: 10% recurring commission is fairly paid, but luggage-storage bookings are low-value, so per-sale earnings are small; no cap statement is published.
reasons.contact_access: No partnerships email is published on the program listing — joining is self-serve through the Tapfiliate portal.
reasons.credibility: Established platform: world's largest luggage-storage network, 1,200+ cities and 1.5M+ ratings at 4.94.
reasons.niche_fit: A genuinely useful service for travel creators making city guides and travel-hack content.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open self-serve sign-up, worldwide, with social media creators an explicitly listed channel.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Social media creators are a named channel, though much of the program is aimed at hosts, venues and travel blogs.

name: Novelship
description: Asia-based marketplace for authentic limited-edition sneakers, streetwear and collectibles. Its affiliate program runs through Impact and is aimed squarely at content creators and influencers: commissions vary by country and customer type up to 5% of the order amount (a ceiling, so no base rate is recorded), with monthly payments, promotional materials and early release information.

evidence.summary: Official program announcement: 'Apply: Sign up through our affiliate portal, Impact', 'Earn a commission up to 5% of order sale amount for each new successful order', and FAQ 'Commission rates vary based on countries & customer type from which purchases are made, up to 5% of order sale amount.' Only a ceiling is published — no base rate — so commission_rate is null. Payments monthly subject to a minimum payout threshold; no earnings-cap statement, so commission_cap is unknown.

The page targets 'content creators, influencers, and anyone passionate about sneakers, streetwear, and collectibles' with a blog, YouTube channel or social presence, offers banners/graphics and early release information, and gives marketing@novelship.com for affiliate inquiries.

reasons.compensation: Only an up-to-5% ceiling is published, varying by country and customer type — a low and uncertain rate, so no base rate is recorded.
reasons.contact_access: A marketing email (marketing@novelship.com) is published on the official program page for affiliate inquiries.
reasons.credibility: Established sneaker marketplace in Asia with an authenticity focus, though less known in the US/EU.
reasons.niche_fit: Sneakers and streetwear are a strong fashion-creator niche.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Free to join via Impact with applications reviewed for fit; no sales targets.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The program explicitly recruits creators, influencers and bloggers and supplies promotional materials.

name: Atlas Swimwear
description: Small swimwear brand running a three-tier creator ladder: an open Explorer community tier, an application-only Ambassador tier paying 10% commission on sales through a personal code (ambassadors must buy a suit and post ATLAS content on TikTok/Instagram), and an invite-or-50-sales Voyager sponsorship tier at 15% commission with free product.

evidence.summary: Official affiliates page: Ambassador tier is application-only; to qualify you must purchase at least one ATLAS bathing suit, actively repost ATLAS videos on TikTok and/or Instagram, create your own ATLAS video and submit a screenshot or DM. Accepted ambassadors get a custom 10%-off follower code and '10% commission on all sales through your code'. The recorded 10% is this Ambassador rate.

Voyager sponsorship tier (sell 50 bathing suits through your code, or be personally invited) pays '15% commission on all referred sales' plus two free bathing suits and 20% off gear. No earnings-cap statement appears on the page, so commission_cap is unknown; no partnerships email is published.

reasons.compensation: 10% Ambassador commission rising to 15% at the sponsorship tier is fair for a small brand; no cap statement is published.
reasons.contact_access: No partnerships email is published — application is via the website/DM only.
reasons.credibility: Very small, young swimwear brand with limited public track record.
reasons.niche_fit: Swimwear is a proven fashion-creator category, though the range is a single product type.
reasons.opportunity_availability: The earning tier is application-only and requires buying a suit and posting brand content before acceptance, which limits availability.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The program is built entirely around creator content — reposting and original TikTok/Instagram videos are explicit requirements.

name: StockX
description: The live bid/ask marketplace for sneakers, streetwear, collectibles, watches and handbags. Its affiliate program runs on Impact: 3% on sneakers, streetwear and collectibles for new customers (1% returning) and 4% on watches and handbags for new customers (2% returning), earned on any bid that converts to a sale within 15 days, backed by a dedicated affiliate team.

evidence.summary: Official StockX program announcement: 'To get started, login or sign up with Impact'; 'Commissions You Earn: Sneakers, Streetwear, & Collectibles: 3% for new customers (first time purchasers), 1% for returning customers. Watches & Handbags: 4% for new customers, 2% for returning customers'; commission is earned on any bid that converts to a sale within 15 days. The recorded 3% is the headline sneakers/streetwear new-customer rate. No earnings-cap statement is published, so commission_cap is unknown.

The announcement (published 2019-07-09) highlights high average order values, monthly newsletters on top-selling products and a 'Dedicated Affiliate Team for collaboration and assistance'. The affiliate contact email shown on the page could not be read in full, so no contact row is recorded.

reasons.compensation: Rates are low — 3% new / 1% returning on sneakers and streetwear — partly offset by high average order values; no cap statement is published.
reasons.contact_access: A dedicated affiliate team is named on the official page, but the contact email could not be read in full, so no email is recorded.
reasons.credibility: One of the largest and best-known resale marketplaces in sneakers and streetwear.
reasons.niche_fit: Sneaker and streetwear drops are a core fashion-creator beat with constant new-release content.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Self-serve sign-up via Impact with a brand-fit review; open to social and media publishers.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The program is pitched at social and media outlets and supplies creative assets, but it is a link-based affiliate program rather than a UGC campaign program.

name: RVshare
description: The largest US peer-to-peer RV rental marketplace, with 100,000+ listed vehicles and average bookings around $699–$900. Its affiliate program is offered through CJ Affiliate (and Travelpayouts), but published rates conflict across sources — 4% per rental on CJ, 5–7% in one directory, 6.5% on Travelpayouts — so no rate is recorded, only the conflict.

evidence.summary: Commission Academy reports the RVshare program as integrated with Commission Junction (CJ Advertiser ID 5126501), paying '4% per referred RV Rental Order' plus '$7 per referred New RV Listing', with 30-day (rental) and 45-day (listing) cookie life and a $900 average order value.

Travelpayouts, which also carries the RVshare offer (US travel projects only, advertiser pre-approval required), publishes a different figure: 'Affiliates can earn 6.5% commission on each completed booking (after check-in) and $12 for every new listing of an RV', with a $699 average booking value. A third directory (Lasso) reports 5–7% per order. Because the published rates conflict (4% vs 5–7% vs 6.5%), commission_rate is null. No earnings-cap statement was found, so commission_cap is unknown.

reasons.compensation: High booking values ($699–$900 average) make even a mid-single-digit rate meaningful, but published rates conflict across sources (4% / 5–7% / 6.5%), so no rate is recorded and compensation is scored cautiously.
reasons.contact_access: No affiliate partnerships email was verified from a fetched source.
reasons.credibility: The largest RV rental marketplace in the US with 100,000+ vehicles and millions of nights booked.
reasons.niche_fit: RV and road-trip content is a strong, growing travel-creator niche.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Available via CJ Affiliate and Travelpayouts, but the advertiser requires pre-approval and the Travelpayouts offer is limited to US travel projects.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The program targets travel publishers and bloggers; creator-specific UGC campaigns are not evidenced.

name: Mountain Warehouse
description: Large UK outdoor retailer selling own-brand clothing and gear for camping, hiking, running, skiing and travel at budget prices. It runs territory affiliate programs through networks including Awin and Rakuten with a 30-day cookie and manual application approval, but its own affiliates page publishes no rate and third-party figures conflict (around 4% in recent directories vs 8.4% in an older listing), so no rate is recorded.

evidence.summary: Official US affiliates page: the program is aimed at sites covering camping, cycling, outdoors, running, skiing, swimming, yoga, walking and travelling; it promises 'High commission rates on every sale you make' without publishing a figure, a 30-day cookie length, and notes 'all affiliate applications are manually approved' and that affiliates join only the territory program matching their audience. No earnings-cap statement is published, so commission_cap is unknown.

Directories conflict on the rate: Lasso reports 4% per sale with a 30-day cookie, Shopper reports up to 3.99%, and an older affjumbo listing reports 8.4%. Groupon reports the program runs 'through Rakuten/Linkshare and AWIN'. Because the figures conflict and the brand publishes none, commission_rate is null.

reasons.compensation: No rate is published by the brand and directory figures conflict (about 4% recently, 8.4% in an older listing), so no rate is recorded and compensation scores low.
reasons.contact_access: No partnerships email is published on the official affiliates page — contact is via territory web forms.
reasons.credibility: One of the UK's largest outdoor retailers with a long trading history and stores internationally.
reasons.niche_fit: Affordable outdoor clothing and gear fits fashion, fitness and travel creators making outdoor content.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Programs run per territory via Awin/Rakuten with manual approval of every application.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The official page addresses website owners placing banners and text links; there is little evidence of creator-specific UGC work.
